what: The gates spike s2 (`reco-q6r`) holds its own measurement to. ADR-003 §4.4 publishes constants it calls 'honest guesses with named prices' and §13.7 defers every one of them to this spike; a gate here is one of those prices written as a number, so that 'did the measurement clear what the document claims' is a lookup instead of a reading-comprehension test. `cargo run -p fathom-analyze --example s2_spike -- --check` re-measures and re-scores them; `tools/gen_segment_tables.py` prints this table into docs/concepts/episode-segmentation.md so the prose cannot disagree with it.
how_gates_are_set: Each claim is stated as what ADR-003 or `e1.3` already published, or as the floor a recommendation has to clear to be worth making at all. A gate that fails is not adjusted to fit the measurement: it is reported failing, and the recommendation has to say what it costs. Two gates (`hook-evidence-*`) are photographs of a world where `e6.1`'s event ingest does not exist yet — they are written to be retired by the ticket that lands it, which is recorded in ADR-003.
scopes: pooled | real | fixture | authored | history:<name> — `real` is Fathom's own history, the only stratum whose clock and subjects were not authored for the corpus, and the stratum a recommendation has to survive on its own.

gates.claim: the cascade ADR-003 §4.2 ships reaches 0.90 boundary F1 on the whole corpus, which is the bar `e1.3`'s acceptance criterion published
the same cascade also clears 0.90 on the pair co-membership measure `crates/fathom-analyze/tests/episodes.rs` gates the corpus at

…and the reason `e1.3`'s own test still passes: on the fixture stratum — the corpus that test measures — the cascade is at 0.86 pair F1, and it is the real and adversarial strata that move the pooled number
the shipped cascade is not worse than the trivial 'every commit is its own episode' partition on the pooled corpus
…and not worse than it on the real stratum either, which is the stratum nobody authored to be friendly
the trivial partition that beats the cascade on F1 hides at least 20 of the corpus's annotated pathologies, which is the proof that boundary F1 alone cannot choose a rule set
turn evidence, where it exists, is never wrong: hook-over-harness-evidence precision is 0.99 or better pooled

the hook rule alone reaches 0.95 pooled boundary F1 — ADR-003 §4.2's confidence 1.0 invites the reading that it is nearly the whole answer, and the corpus refuses it: with no evidence on either side of a boundary TB6 keeps the commits together, and 76 annotated turns get swallowed

as shipped, the hook rule has essentially no evidence on real agent-driven history: with commit-carried evidence only, its recall on the real stratum is at most 0.05. This is a photograph of the world before `e6.1`, and the ticket that lands event ingest is expected to retire it rather than leave it quietly true

ADR-003 rung 3 (`Fathom-Episode:` trailer, confidence 0.9) does work when somebody writes the trailer it reads: on the history authored to carry it, trailers-plus-message-shape reaches 0.90 boundary F1

…and everywhere else that rule is dead: on the pooled corpus the trailer-plus-message-shape strategy finds at most 10 % of the true boundaries, because the trailer it reads is written by nothing in this repository or the fixture corpus
for a time-and-author strategy the best gap on this corpus is at or below 20 minutes, so the published 30 is not the optimum the ADR guessed it was

the shipped cascade's pooled optimum gap is at or below 20 minutes too (measured 10), so `episode.time_gap_minutes` is not sitting near its optimum by luck — it is not near an optimum at all, and §4.4's 30 is a value whose measured leverage is smaller than its documentation weight

the recommended rule set reaches 0.90 pooled boundary F1 at the published 30-minute gap, which is what licenses leaving the constant alone: once a per-commit claim carries the boundary, the clock stops being the instrument

the recommended rule set (subject-claim above the clock, session-qualified turn ids) beats the shipped cascade by at least 0.05 pooled boundary F1 — a change to a documented cascade has to pay for the churn
…and it beats it on the real stratum by at least 0.02, because a recommendation that only works on authored histories is a recommendation about the corpus
the recommended rule set hides no more annotated pathologies than the shipped cascade does pooled
the shipped cascade hides at most three annotated pathologies on the real stratum, which is where a hidden pathology is a real one
the recommended rule set hides at most two on the real stratum, and both are of the kind no git signal can see

the subject-claim signal fires on at most 2 of the 60 within-turn adjacencies in the corpus: a leading tracker token is evidence rather than a guess, and it is the only added signal that costs no false boundaries
ADR-003 §4.3's claim that a conventional-type change is the weakest splitting signal in the set is confirmed rather than assumed: message-shape finds at most 5 true boundaries in the whole corpus
the recommended rule set swallows fewer annotated turns than the shipped cascade, which is the failure direction that removes work from the queue

expected_semantics: Every gate declares `expected`: `pass` or `fail`. A gate that surprises us in either direction fails the contract test — a claim that starts passing has to be re-read as well as one that fails. The `fail` gates are the spike's findings, not its defects: they are the prices ADR-003 §4.4 and `e1.3` published that this measurement refuses to let stand.
